answer: A sybil farm profits by letting puppets trade mostly with each other, manufacturing history inside a closed loop. Count only bridge work: each epoch a public beacon randomly pairs identities from clusters with almost no shared history, so a provider cannot choose its own sock puppets as customers. The buyer pays on delivery, then must echo confirmation days later that the deliverable is still in use; unconfirmed and self-looped work earns nothing. Faking genuine use across many random outsiders costs more real work than the reward pays.
